evidence: Through field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) and atomic force microscopy (AFM) observations, we confirmed that the amorphous SnS2 films were smooth and were in close contact with the substrate. X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) analyses showed that amorphous SnS2 films were obtained when the preparation temperature was below 140 ◦C. The optical properties of the amorphous SnS2 films grown at different temperatures were measured in the UV–Vis range of 300 to 1400 nm. The photocurrent response was evaluated using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS).
